item.title: Maria Bartiromo Is Out at Fox News
item.description: The host, who appeared on Fox Business and Fox News, had been with the network for more than 12 years.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wemple
item.media:description: Fox did not give a reason for Maria Bartiromo’s abrupt departure. She has been an ardent supporter of President Trump.

item.title: Bessent Blames Ukraine for High Energy Prices
item.description: After meeting with Russia’s finance minister, the Treasury secretary said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure were contributing to a global energy shock driven mainly by the U.S. war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump (Book)
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is facing a complicated challenge as he tries to cool global energy prices while increasing economic pressure on Iran.

item.title: Leon Black Sues Congressional Panel Investigating Epstein
item.description: The billionaire skipped a deposition on Thursday and filed a lawsuit seeking to block a House committee’s subpoenas demanding nondisclosure agreements he may have made with women.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Goldstein and Michael Gold
item.category: House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
item.media:description: Leon Black, left, leaving the Rayburn House Office Building in June after he cut short his interview with the House Oversight Committee about Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: The Athletic Says Dianna Russini’s Relationship With Mike Vrabel Violated Its Standards
item.description: The New York Times-owned publication said the relationship between its former reporter Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel of the Patriots gave the appearance of a conflict of interest.
item.dc:creator: Ken Belson and Katherine Rosman
item.media:description: Dianna Russini at an N.F.L. game in September 2019. As an N.F.L. insider, she was focused on getting scoops about players and coaches.

item.title: Schools Giving Aid to Minority Students Could Lose Tax Exemptions Under Trump’s New Rules
item.description: The Treasury Department released rules that would prevent schools with race-based programs from qualifying for tax-exempt status, a threat to both higher education and other private schools.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren and Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Schools like Harvard could be at risk of losing their tax-exempt status under the new rules.

item.title: U.S. Trade Gap Ballooned in July
item.description: The trade deficit bounced back up last month as spending on data centers to feed the A.I. boom drove up imports.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson

item.title: Rate Rise in Play as Fed Officials Await Inflation Data
item.description: Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, sounded optimistic about inflation’s trajectory but indicated he would support higher rates if progress does not continue.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Christopher Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, said he was looking for evidence that showed inflation was continuing to abate.

item.title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal
item.description: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang, Lauren Hirsch and Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, has overseen the company as its quarterly profits have increased tenfold. The company is spending those resources on acquisitions, including of Hugging Face.

item.title: Oil Jumps for Fourth Straight Day and Diesel Nears Record High
item.description: This week’s renewed strikes by the United States and Iran strain the flow of energy and diminish expectations the disruption will end soon.

item.title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
item.description: When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith

item.title: Why the Courts Are Hesitant to Punish Tech Giants Like Meta and Google
item.description: After finding antitrust violations, federal courts have been reluctant to impose harsh sanctions. They fear meddling in markets where technology is racing ahead.
item.dc:creator: Steve Lohr
item.media:credit: Kelsey McClellan for The New York Times
item.media:description: Creating effective remedies is difficult for the courts, particularly because of the rapid pace of change in the tech industry.

item.title: Trump Puts Tariffs of Up to 100% on Foreign-Made Drones
item.description: In addition, the F.C.C. is weighing stiff restrictions on common drone technology such as thermal imaging and aerosol spraying.
item.dc:creator: Farah Stockman
item.media:description: A drone made by DJI, a company based in Shenzhen, China, flying over a farm in Hickory, N.C., in 2024.

item.title: Uber and Wayve to Start Testing Robotaxis in London
item.description: Uber and the British start-up Wayve are the latest to start testing autonomous cars in one of the world’s largest markets for ride-hailing services.
item.dc:creator: Adam Satariano
item.media:credit: Andrew Testa for The New York Times

item.title: Southwest to Open Premium Airport Lounges Across the Country
item.description: The airline said that lounges in Baltimore, Honolulu, Nashville and Austin, Texas, would debut starting late next year, and that seven more were in the works.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung and Niraj Chokshi
item.media:description: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, in Texas, is one of four airports that could be getting a Southwest Airlines premium lounge starting late next year.

item.title: Trump’s Tactics to Lower Beef Prices and Appease Ranchers Fall Short
item.description: The Agriculture Department offered new initiatives for ranchers after President Trump said he would import more beef. The moves aren’t a quick fix.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Draper
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times
item.media:description: The U.S. cattle supply is at its smallest level since 1951.

item.title: Chevron Expansion in Venezuela Extends U.S. Influence Over Oil Riches
item.description: The U.S. energy giant, which stayed in the country after other Western companies left, will invest $7 billion in the country to more than double its production there.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott
item.category: North American Blue Energy Partners Inc
item.media:description: Oil infrastructure in Cabimas, Venezuela. Chevron’s expansion is separate from President Trump’s deal for control of oil reserves in the country.

item.title: Investors Still on Edge Over War, Debt and Inflation

item.title: Employer Health Costs Are Expected to Spike in 2027
item.description: A new U.S. survey anticipates an average increase of 11 percent unless benefits are cut, the highest rate in decades. Other findings also predict a sharp rise.
item.dc:creator: Reed Abelson
item.media:credit: Morgan Lieberman for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S. employers are bracing for what looks to be the sharpest increase in health care costs in more than two decades.

item.title: Global Bond Rates Are Rising. What Should You Do Now?

item.title: FiveThirtyEight’s Podcast Hosts Reunite for a New Show
item.description: Nate Silver, Clare Malone and Galen Druke will host “Still Counting,” a nonpartisan politics show — on a decidedly partisan podcast network.
item.dc:creator: Katie Robertson
item.media:description: Galen Druke, left, Clare Malone and Nate Silver are hoping to resurrect the spirt of their former podcast at Crooked Media.

item.title: Saturday Evening Post Will Stop Printing After 205 Years
item.description: The magazine, famous for publishing Jack London stories and Norman Rockwell art, will continue online.

item.media:description: The Saturday Evening Post cover from May 29, 1943.

item.title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
item.description: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.
item.dc:creator: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.media:description: Apple’s more recent iPhone models include the ability to communicate with emergency services by text chat over a satellite connection, as well as a demonstration mode.

item.title: Inside the Fight Against a Flesh-Eating Fly in Mexico
item.description: For the first time in a year, the U.S.-Mexico border partly reopened to cattle imports following a screwworm infestation across the region. The battle against the flesh-eating fly has only just begun deep in Mexico.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner and Luis Antonio Rojas
item.media:credit: Luis Antonio Rojas for The New York Times
item.media:description: New World screwworm flies in a cage at a facility in Metapa, Mexico, that that produces sterile flies, which when released into the wild slowly reduce the population size.

item.title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
item.description: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe and Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Clayton Steward for The New York Times
item.media:description: Organizers of the recall vote said the councilman, John Perkins, had failed to engage the public while the city negotiated with the developer of a data center project.

item.title: Bill Simmons’s Co-Hosts Are Tired of His A.I. Antics
item.description: The founder of The Ringer is taking flak for using artificial intelligence to conjure opinions from the deceased film critic Roger Ebert. Ads from OpenAI have recently run on the show.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:credit: Mike Windle/Getty Images for Vanity Fair
item.media:description: Film buffs are complaining that the podcast host Bill Simmons used artificial intelligence to approximate the opinions of the critic Roger Ebert, who died in 2013.

item.title: Ozempic Maker Novo Nordisk’s Investors Are Nervously Looking Into the Future

item.title: Satsuki Katayama, the Woman at the Center of Japan’s Currency Fight

item.title: Bond Sell-Off Threatens to Squeeze Borrowers Around the World

item.title: Shein’s Lackluster Debut Shows a Fast-Fashion Model Left Behind

item.title: Expedia Fights Off Claim for Damages by Cuban Exile Families

item.title: IRS Audit Revenue Has Plummeted Under Trump, Watchdog Finds

item.title: Kalshi Permanently Bars George Santos From the Platform

item.title: Private Equity Wants to Invest in College Sports. Some Schools Are Wary.
item.description: As desperate as many athletic programs are for money, they are proceeding cautiously when it comes to deals with private equity.
item.dc:creator: Joe Drape
